q: A passenger in an intoxicated state creates a nuisance in the coach and refuses to quieten down. Drunkenness or nuisance by a person in a train or on railway premises is punishable under:

options.A: Section 141 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.B: Section 145 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.C: Section 167 of the Railways Act, 1989
options.D: Section 143 of the Railways Act, 1989

e: Section 145 of the Railways Act, 1989 punishes a person found in a state of intoxication, or committing a nuisance or using obscene or abusive language, in a train or on railway premises.

q: For a passenger's claim to fall within the definition of an 'untoward incident' under Section 123 of the Railways Act, 1989, it is enough that the incident is:

options.A: Detention of a train on account of fog
options.B: Failure of signalling equipment at a station
options.C: A terrorist act affecting a passenger in a train or within station premises
options.D: Cancellation of a train for operational reasons

e: Section 123(c) of the Railways Act, 1989 includes a terrorist act affecting a passenger in a train or within station premises within the definition of an untoward incident.

q: The 'running speed' of a train is worked out on a different basis from its average speed, in that running speed is computed:

options.A: By including the time of halts at all intermediate stations
options.B: By including the detention at the destination terminal
options.C: On the basis of route kilometres divided by the number of trains
options.D: Excluding the time of halts at intermediate stations en route

e: Running speed is computed excluding the time of halts at intermediate stations en route; average speed includes those halts, which is the basic distinction between the two measures.

q: When a division reports its daily position, the wagons counted in its 'wagon holding' are:

options.A: The wagons physically present on the lines of that railway, irrespective of the railway which owns them
options.B: The wagons owned by that railway, wherever they may be running
options.C: The wagons loaded at the stations of that railway during the day
options.D: The wagons under repair in the workshops of that railway

e: Wagon holding in the daily position counts the wagons physically present on the lines of the railway at that time, irrespective of which railway owns them.

q: A low-rated traffic which faces stiff road competition is proposed to be accepted below its fully distributed cost. Under differential pricing in the railway tariff, such traffic may be accepted at a rate based on:

options.A: The fully distributed cost of the service in all cases
options.B: Marginal (out-of-pocket) cost, so long as the traffic makes a contribution towards the fixed costs
options.C: The average cost of all coaching and goods services together
options.D: The cost of working the most expensive route

e: Differential pricing allows traffic facing road competition to be accepted at a rate based on marginal or out-of-pocket cost, so long as it contributes something towards fixed costs.

q: A child aged eight years is taken in a reserved coach and the family does not demand a separate berth for the child. The fare chargeable for the child is:

options.A: Full fare
options.B: No fare, the child being carried free
options.C: Half fare
options.D: One-third of the adult fare

e: A child aged five to twelve travelling without a separate berth is charged half fare under the Coaching Tariff child fare rules; full fare applies only when a separate berth is sought.

q: A Private Freight Terminal differs from an ordinary railway goods shed in that it is normally developed:

options.A: On railway land, entirely at the cost of the Railways
options.B: Within the circulating area of a passenger station
options.C: Only at a gateway port
options.D: On private (non-railway) land by a private operator, with rail connectivity provided by the Railways

e: A Private Freight Terminal is normally developed on private, non-railway land by a private operator, with rail connectivity provided by the Railways, unlike a railway goods shed.

q: A passenger cancels a ticket which is still waitlisted, and another cancels one in RAC; in both cases the amount deducted from the fare on cancellation is:

options.A: Clerkage charge only
options.B: The prescribed cancellation charge for a confirmed ticket
options.C: The reservation charge together with the cancellation charge
options.D: Fifty per cent of the fare in every case

e: On cancellation of waitlisted and RAC tickets, which are not confirmed, only the clerkage charge is deducted under the refund rules, not the cancellation charge for confirmed tickets.

q: A passenger in AC 2-Tier is asked to pay separately for the bedding supplied to him and disputes the demand. In AC 2-Tier class, the bedding supplied to passengers is:

options.A: Charged for separately in all trains
options.B: Supplied free of charge, its cost being included in the fare
options.C: Not supplied at all
options.D: Supplied only against a refundable security deposit

e: In AC 2-Tier, bedding is supplied free of charge because its cost is included in the fare under the Coaching Tariff, so no separate bedding charge can be demanded from the passenger.

q: A reservation clerk is asked whether a Tatkal booking can be made in the highest classes of a train. The Tatkal scheme for reservation is NOT applicable in:

options.A: AC 2-Tier class
options.B: AC 3-Tier class
options.C: First AC and Executive Class
options.D: Sleeper class

e: The Tatkal scheme does not apply in First AC and Executive Class under the reservation rules; it operates in other reserved classes including AC 2-Tier, AC 3-Tier and Sleeper.

q: The extent to which the capacity of a busy section is actually being used by the trains run over it is expressed as:

options.A: Gross Tonne Kilometres per route kilometre of the section
options.B: The number of trains run per station on the section
options.C: Earnings per route kilometre of the section
options.D: The percentage of the section's capacity utilised by the trains actually run

e: Line capacity utilisation is expressed as the percentage of a section's capacity actually utilised by the trains run over it, showing the extent to which the busy section is used.

q: Under the Traffic Accounts Management System (TAMS), the discipline imposed on corrections to station data is that:

options.A: All modifications in the station data are routed through the Error Sheet module, so that accountal and traceability are ensured
options.B: The manual submission of station balance sheets continues as before, the system being used only for statistical statements
options.C: Stations may alter their figures freely in the system without any record
options.D: Modifications are made only by the Travelling Inspector of Accounts during inspection

e: Under TAMS all modifications in station data are routed through the Error Sheet module, so that every correction is accounted for and traceable and no figure is altered without record.

q: A large station collects earnings on behalf of several smaller stations; in the Traffic Accounts Office, those collections are checked with:

options.A: The balance sheets of the collecting station alone
options.B: The credits taken by those other stations
options.C: The cash remittance notes of the collecting station
options.D: The error sheets issued to the collecting station

e: Collections made by a station on behalf of other stations are checked in the Traffic Accounts Office with the credits taken by those other stations, to ensure complete accountal.

q: A passenger surrenders a ticket he has not used and is refunded the fare after deduction of clerkage charges. The document invariably issued to the passenger in connection with such a refund is a:

options.A: Excess Fare Ticket
options.B: Ticket Deposit Receipt
options.C: Money Receipt
options.D: Error Sheet

e: When an unused ticket is surrendered and fare refunded after deducting clerkage, a Money Receipt is invariably issued to the passenger as the document evidencing the refund.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The avoidable cost of a traffic service is the cost which would be saved if that service were withdrawn or discontinued.
2. The avoidable cost of a service is its fully distributed cost, including all overheads, whether they would be saved or not.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 1 only

e: Avoidable cost is only the cost saved on withdrawal of a service, so statement 1 is correct; fully distributed cost including unavoidable overheads, in statement 2, is not avoidable cost.

q: The periodical statement of gross earnings of Indian Railways is not built up from the balance sheets; its basic document is the:

options.A: Advance Statement of Gross Earnings and Traffic Handled
options.B: Station Balance Sheet
options.C: Passenger Classification return
options.D: Accounts Office Balance Sheet

e: The periodical statement of gross earnings is built up from the Advance Statement of Gross Earnings and Traffic Handled furnished by zonal railways, not from station balance sheets.

q:
Consider the following statements about the passenger classification return rendered by a station:
1. The return shows the commencing and closing numbers of tickets.
2. The return also shows the index numbers of non-issued tickets and the amounts derived from full-fare tickets and concession tickets.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The passenger classification return shows commencing and closing ticket numbers and also index numbers of non-issued tickets and amounts from full-fare and concession tickets, so both are correct.

q:
A finance officer is explaining to a probationer why the two aggregates shown in the annual results of his railway do not tally with each other. Consider the following statements in this regard:
1. Gross earnings of the Railways comprise the coaching, goods and sundry other earnings accrued during the period.
2. Gross receipts, as distinct from gross earnings, also take into account the suspense accounts connected with traffic transactions.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Gross earnings comprise coaching, goods and sundry other earnings accrued, while gross receipts also take into account traffic suspense accounts, so the two aggregates differ and both statements are correct.

q: Handling charges and similar amounts which a station pays out under proper authority on behalf of the Railways are not kept outside its accounts; they are brought into the Station Balance Sheet as:

options.A: Error sheets
options.B: Transfer certificates
options.C: Cash remittance notes
options.D: Paid vouchers

e: Amounts paid out by a station under proper authority on behalf of the Railways, such as handling charges, are brought into the Station Balance Sheet as paid vouchers supporting the payments.

q: Some small stations do not render a balance sheet of their own at all. Such stations, whose transactions are accounted for through a nominated balance sheet station, are known as:

options.A: Non-Balance Sheet stations
options.B: Out agencies
options.C: Flag stations
options.D: City booking offices

e: Stations that render no balance sheet of their own and whose transactions are accounted through a nominated balance sheet station are known as Non-Balance Sheet stations.

q: A passenger who wants to lodge a grievance about a dirty coach and also track what action is taken on it is directed to a single integrated facility of Indian Railways for registering, tracking and resolving passenger complaints and grievances. That facility is:

options.A: Rail Madad
options.B: National Train Enquiry System
options.C: Freight Operations Information System
options.D: Traffic Accounts Management System

e: Rail Madad is the integrated facility of Indian Railways for registering, tracking and resolving passenger complaints and grievances through a single portal, helpline and app interface.

q: An automobile manufacturer wants dedicated carriage for cars in wagons designed specially for that traffic, without buying train paths from anyone else. Under the Automobile Freight Train Operator scheme, such an operator:

options.A: Carries automobiles free of charge in passenger trains
options.B: Invests in specially designed wagons for the carriage of automobiles and pays haulage charges to the Railways
options.C: Leases brake vans from the Railways for road transport of cars
options.D: Manufactures automobiles in the production units of the Railways

e: Under the Automobile Freight Train Operator scheme the operator invests in specially designed wagons for carriage of automobiles and pays haulage charges to the Railways for their movement.

q: A Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevak sells unreserved tickets from his own premises away from the station and a dispute arises about how his sales enter the railway accounts. The tickets sold by such a sevak are accounted for:

options.A: Directly in the books of the Railway Board
options.B: By the sevak himself, without any account being rendered to the Railways
options.C: Through the station to which the sevak is linked, on the lines of station accounts
options.D: Only in the accounts of the Divisional Commercial Branch

e: Tickets sold by a Jansadharan Ticket Booking Sevak are accounted through the station to which the sevak is linked, on the lines of station accounts, so the Railways account for all his sales.

q: A daily commuter who has been buying paper season tickets asks whether he can instead get his season ticket on his phone. In regard to season tickets through the UTS mobile application, the correct position is that:

options.A: Season tickets cannot be issued or renewed through the application in any case
options.B: Only single journey tickets can be booked through the application
options.C: Season tickets issued through the application are valid only in suburban sections of one railway
options.D: Monthly and quarterly season tickets can be issued and renewed through the UTS mobile application

e: Monthly and quarterly season tickets can be issued and renewed through the UTS mobile application, in addition to paper season tickets at booking counters, under the mobile ticketing rules.

q: At a destination station, the staff have reason to believe that a consignor has described the contents of his consignment falsely in order to pay less freight. In such a case, the Railways may:

options.A: Open and examine the consignment in the presence of the consignor, the consignee or their representative, in order to verify the declaration
options.B: Deliver the consignment without any examination in all cases
options.C: Confiscate the consignment immediately without any examination
options.D: Return the consignment to the forwarding station at the cost of the destination station

e: Where false description of a consignment is suspected, the Railways may open and examine it in the presence of the consignor, consignee or their representative to verify the declaration, under Section 66.

q: A passenger keeps his ticket in his bag and, when the ticket checking staff ask to see it, says he will show it only on reaching his destination. A passenger travelling by train is in fact required to:

options.A: Produce his ticket only at the destination station
options.B: Hand over his ticket permanently to the conductor at the start of the journey
options.C: Purchase a fresh ticket whenever his ticket is demanded for check
options.D: Produce his ticket or pass for examination on demand by a railway servant authorised in this behalf, failing which he is liable to be treated as travelling without a proper ticket

e: Section 55 of the Railways Act, 1989 requires a passenger to produce his ticket or pass on demand by an authorised railway servant, failing which he is treated as travelling without a proper ticket.

q: Mid-journey, a passenger with a reserved ticket decides that he wants to go on to a station beyond the one named on his ticket. He can have his journey so extended by:

options.A: Travelling beyond the destination without paying anything further
options.B: Paying double the fare for the additional distance as a penalty in all cases
options.C: Getting his journey extended on payment of the fare for the additional distance, through the ticket checking staff, before reaching his destination
options.D: Surrendering his ticket and booking a fresh ticket from the originating station

e: A passenger can get his journey extended before reaching his destination by paying the fare for the additional distance through the ticket checking staff, who endorse the extension on the ticket.

q: A probationer is asked who brings out the annual publication that sums up the performance of Indian Railways for the year, including earnings, traffic and statistics. The 'Year Book' of Indian Railways is published by:

options.A: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: The NITI Aayog
options.C: The respective zonal railways for their own systems only
options.D: The Ministry of Railways (Railway Board)

e: The Year Book of Indian Railways, the annual publication summing up earnings, traffic, statistics and performance for the year, is published by the Ministry of Railways, that is the Railway Board.

q: A passenger reaches the station to find that his train is delayed by more than the prescribed period, and he decides not to travel by it at all. In regard to refund in such a case, the position is that:

options.A: No refund is admissible in any case
options.B: Full refund of the fare is admissible to the passenger
options.C: Only the reservation charge is refunded to the passenger
options.D: Refund is admissible only through the Railway Claims Tribunal

e: If a train is delayed by more than the prescribed period and the passenger does not travel by it, full refund of fare is admissible under the refund rules, without the normal cancellation deduction.

q: A student who is entitled to a fare concession finds that the concession has not been applied to every rupee he paid for his ticket. A concession in passenger fares admissible under the rules is calculated:

options.A: On the total fare including all supplementary charges
options.B: On the reservation charge and the superfast charge only
options.C: On the basic fare only, the other charges being payable in full
options.D: On the Tatkal charges, where the ticket is booked under the Tatkal scheme

e: Fare concession under the Coaching Tariff is calculated on the basic fare only; reservation, superfast and other supplementary charges on the ticket are payable in full by the passenger.

q: A booking clerk explains to a trainee that the reservation charge collected on a reserved ticket is not the same amount for every passenger. The reservation charge levied on a reserved ticket:

options.A: Varies according to the class of travel
options.B: Is uniform for all classes of travel
options.C: Is levied only on tickets in the air-conditioned classes
options.D: Is levied only on Tatkal tickets

e: The reservation charge on a reserved ticket varies according to the class of travel under the Coaching Tariff schedule of charges, and is not a uniform amount for all classes.

q: For a journey, the straight-line distance between two stations is shorter than the distance over the line on which the train actually runs. Passenger fares for a train journey are charged on the basis of:

options.A: The shortest road distance between the two stations
options.B: The distance by the route by which the train actually travels
options.C: The straight-line (crow-fly) distance between the two stations
options.D: A uniform distance slab for all trains on the section

e: Passenger fares are charged on the distance by the route by which the train actually travels between the stations, not on straight-line, road or any uniform slab distance.

q: A trader who once complained about the reasonableness of a freight rate asks which body now deals with the work that the old Railway Rates Tribunal used to do. The functions of the erstwhile Railway Rates Tribunal now vest in:

options.A: The Central Administrative Tribunal
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: The Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
options.D: The Railway Claims Tribunal

e: The functions of the erstwhile Railway Rates Tribunal, which dealt with complaints about reasonableness of freight rates, now vest in the Railway Claims Tribunal after the merger of the tribunals.

q: Two passengers travel the same distance in the same class, one by an ordinary passenger train and the other by a Mail/Express train. For the same class and the same distance, the fare charged for travel by a Mail/Express train, as compared with the fare by an ordinary passenger train, is:

options.A: Higher
options.B: The same
options.C: Lower
options.D: Charged only on the return journey

e: For the same class and distance, travel by a Mail or Express train is charged at a higher fare than by an ordinary passenger train, reflecting the higher Mail and Express fare basis in the tariff.

q: A passenger brings his motor cycle to the parcel office for booking and is told that one safety condition must be met before it can be accepted. Before a motor cycle is accepted for booking as luggage or as a parcel, it is essential that:

options.A: It is insured against theft during transit
options.B: It is packed in a wooden crate
options.C: A security deposit is paid by the consignor
options.D: The fuel in its tank is completely drained out

e: Before a motor cycle is accepted as luggage or parcel, the fuel in its tank must be completely drained out as a safety condition, to remove the fire risk from petrol during carriage.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Busy Season Charge on goods traffic:
1. The Busy Season Charge on goods traffic is levied at the rate of 10 per cent of the base freight rate.
2. The busy season for goods traffic is the period from October to June.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The busy season for goods traffic is October to June, so statement 2 is correct; the Busy Season Charge is not 10 per cent of base freight, so statement 1 as stated is not correct.

q: A waitlisted passenger's status on his PNR is shown by a code indicating that he is waiting against the Tatkal quota of the train. In the Passenger Reservation System, the abbreviation TQWL denotes:

options.A: Train Quota Wait List
options.B: Terminal Quota Wait List
options.C: Through Quota Wait List
options.D: Tatkal Quota Wait List

e: In PRS terminology TQWL denotes Tatkal Quota Wait List, the waitlist of passengers booked under the Tatkal quota who could not get confirmed Tatkal accommodation.

q: A freight customer who cannot afford to wait for his turn in the normal course wants wagons ahead of other indents. Under the Premium Indent Scheme of the Railways, a freight customer can obtain:

options.A: Wagons on a priority or out-of-turn basis, on payment of a premium over the normal wagon registration fee
options.B: A rebate in freight for loading traffic in the empty-flow direction
options.C: Exemption from demurrage at goods terminals
options.D: Free weighment of all his consignments

e: Under the Premium Indent Scheme a freight customer can get wagons on a priority or out-of-turn basis on payment of a premium over the normal wagon registration fee, ahead of ordinary indents.

q: A consignor booking a parcel is asked to pay the parcel charges at the booking counter itself, and not at the other end. In parcel traffic, the parcel charges are:

options.A: Required to be prepaid at the time of booking
options.B: Always collected at the destination station as 'to-pay' charges
options.C: Billed to the consignee month by month
options.D: Recovered only after weighment of the parcels at the destination

e: In parcel traffic the parcel charges are required to be prepaid at the time of booking under the Coaching Tariff, and parcels are not normally booked on a to-pay basis at destination.

q: A passenger who has to make a long-distance journey by an unreserved train three days later asks how early he can buy his ticket. Advance booking of unreserved tickets for long-distance journeys is permitted at stations and through the Unreserved Ticketing System:

options.A: Up to 7 days in advance for all journeys
options.B: Only on the day of the journey
options.C: Up to 30 days in advance for all journeys
options.D: Up to 3 days in advance, where the distance of the journey exceeds 200 kilometres

e: Advance booking of unreserved tickets is permitted up to 3 days in advance where the journey distance exceeds 200 kilometres, while shorter journeys are booked on the day of travel.

q: Large quantities of milk move every day from the producing areas to the big cities for distribution there. Milk traffic from the producing centres to the metropolitan cities is carried by the Railways in:

options.A: Special milk tank wagons
options.B: Ordinary open wagons
options.C: Insulated parcel vans only
options.D: Passenger coaches attached to mail trains

e: Milk traffic from producing centres to metropolitan cities is carried in special milk tank wagons provided for bulk carriage of milk, not in ordinary open wagons or parcel vans.

q: A consignment remains with the Railways even after its transit has ended, and a question arises about the legal capacity in which the Railways then hold it. Under the Railways Act, 1989, after the termination of transit, the responsibility of the railway administration in respect of the goods entrusted to it is that of:

options.A: An insurer of the goods
options.B: A bailee under the Indian Contract Act, 1872
options.C: A common carrier with absolute liability
options.D: A warehouseman without any liability

e: Under Section 99 of the Railways Act, 1989, after termination of transit the railway administration holds the goods as a bailee under the Indian Contract Act, 1872, with a bailee's responsibility.

q: A probationer is asked which organisation has built and now operates the Dedicated Freight Corridors of the Railways. The Dedicated Freight Corridors have been built and are operated by:

options.A: The zonal railways through which they pass
options.B: Container Corporation of India Limited
options.C: Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited
options.D: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited

e: The Dedicated Freight Corridors have been built and are operated by the Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited, the special purpose company set up for that project.

q: Some train accidents are classed apart from others because of the gravity of what follows from them. 'Consequential train accidents' on the Railways are those train accidents which:

options.A: Have serious repercussions in the form of loss of human life or injury to persons, damage to railway property or interruption of through traffic
options.B: Involve only departmental (material) trains
options.C: Occur only at manned level crossing gates
options.D: Result in no damage to railway property at all

e: Consequential train accidents are those having serious repercussions like loss of life or injury, damage to railway property or interruption to through traffic, which marks their gravity.

q: At a reservation office, a passenger is helped by a person who is not a railway employee but is authorised to book reserved tickets for passengers for a prescribed service charge. Such Rail Travellers' Service Agents (RTSAs) on Indian Railways are:

options.A: Agents authorised to sell unreserved tickets at halt stations
options.B: Contractors engaged for the loading and unloading of goods at stations
options.C: Agents licensed by the Railways to book reserved tickets on behalf of passengers, charging them a prescribed service charge
options.D: Staff deputed by travel agencies to work at reservation counters

e: Rail Travellers' Service Agents are agents licensed by the Railways to book reserved tickets on behalf of passengers and to charge them the prescribed service charge for that service.

q: A customer wants a parcel collected from his door and delivered at the addressee's door through a combined rail and postal service. The 'Joint Parcel Product' (JPP) service for door-to-door delivery of parcels is a joint initiative of Indian Railways and:

options.A: The Department of Telecommunications
options.B: The Department of Posts (India Post)
options.C: The National Highways Authority of India
options.D: The Container Corporation of India

e: The Joint Parcel Product for door-to-door parcel delivery, combining rail carriage with collection and delivery, is a joint initiative of Indian Railways and the Department of Posts, India Post.

q: A steel plant books an entire train-load of its product at one station for carriage to one single station at the other end. In goods traffic, such a 'block rake' means:

options.A: A rake which is blocked for departmental use during emergencies
options.B: A rake formed of wagons belonging to different owning railways
options.C: A full train-load consignment booked by one party from one station to a single destination station
options.D: A rake detained at a station for want of movement instructions

e: A block rake is a full train-load consignment booked by one party from one station to a single destination station, moving as one rake without piecemeal loading or unloading en route.

q: Stations deposit their remittances at the focal point branches of the bank, and the Cash Office has to give credit for those remittances in the accounts. Credits for remittances deposited by stations at the focal point branches of the bank are afforded in the Cash Office on the basis of:

options.A: The Station Balance Sheet alone
options.B: The scrolls/returns of remittances received from the bank
options.C: The error sheets issued by the Traffic Accounts Office
options.D: The monthly statement rendered by the Station Master

e: Credits for station remittances deposited at focal point bank branches are afforded in the Cash Office on the basis of the scrolls or returns of remittances received from the bank.

q:
Consider the following statements about goods traffic exchanged with foreign railways:
1. Through goods traffic is exchanged with the neighbouring foreign railways, such as those of Bangladesh and Nepal, at nominated interchange points.
2. The earnings of such international traffic are apportioned and settled between the railway administrations concerned on agreed principles.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Through goods traffic is exchanged with neighbouring foreign railways like Bangladesh and Nepal at nominated interchange points, and its earnings are apportioned on agreed principles, so both are correct.

q: A goods clerk breaking up a freight bill for a customer explains that the total freight he pays is not a single distance charge alone. Goods freight is correctly made up of:

options.A: Only the line-haul charge based on distance, terminal services being rendered free
options.B: Terminal charges for the services rendered at the terminals and line-haul charges based on the distance over which the goods are carried
options.C: Only the terminal charges at the originating station, the carriage itself being free
options.D: Demurrage and wharfage charges, together with the siding charges of the station

e: Goods freight consists of terminal charges for services at the terminals and line-haul charges based on the distance carried, the two components together making up the total freight charged.
